rows.source: TrueHD object-presentation channels / JOC reconstructed object signals
rows.damf: CAF 24-bit BE, one channel per element
rows.adm: `data` chunk 24-bit LE, one track per element
rows.classification: sample-exact
rows.note: 590 of 590 declared DAMF/ADM track pairs are sample-identical (SHA-256 of the samples equal) over 25 inputs including the whole-film Pi (242322080 frames); the full pairing matrix confirms every declared pair (True). The ADM carries exactly the PCM the decoder produced; JOC objects are the decoder's reconstruction, not the master (differential claim).

rows.internal: bed slots, conformed to 7.1.2 by default
rows.adm: DirectSpeakers tracks first, `RC_*` labels
rows.classification: label-confirmed
rows.note: LFE is sample-identical in every input; harness C21 codes the bed as Rss, Lss, LFE and the tones land under the matching labels with conform on ([None, None, None, 100.0, 600.0, 500.0, None, None, None, None, 440.0]) and off. LFE is identified only by the `RC_LFE` label and position [-1,1,-1] (profile table 10); a BS.2127 renderer does not recognise that label (EAR warning) - a profile-level interoperability limit shared with Dolby's own files.

rows.source: element order: beds, ISF, dynamic objects
rows.adm: `chna` -> ATU -> AT -> AS -> AC chain
rows.note: Every chna entry resolves through a unique UID/track/stream/channel chain to the audioObject that owns it; no dangling, duplicate or orphan node in any file (25 inputs, 0 findings on the whole film).

rows.adm: 1:1 for beds and dynamic objects; ISF absent
rows.classification: an ISF programme is refused, or written without its ISF objects and declared on request (D2; see ISF row)
rows.note: Bed, dynamic-object and total element counts agree between OAMD, DAMF and ADM on every input (all corpus beds are LFE-only). Codec channels, JOC reconstructed signals, OAMD programme objects and ADM audioObjects are counted separately in the report. Remediation C13b (`--isf drop`): adm `isf-dropped` 4, damf `isf-dropped` 4.

rows.adm: `Atmos_Obj_k` / `AO_100b+`, one channel format per object
rows.note: No object changes track or id through any programme: block tiling is gapless and sorted for every object (gaps 0, overlaps 0 on real material), and the PCM under each object's channel format is identical to the DAMF element from first to last sample.

rows.adm: `position X/Y`, 10 decimals
rows.note: 0 value mismatches at float32 precision over 36434 matched events; against the raw OAMD dump the mapping holds within 9.7e-05 (the dump's 4 decimals) on 6 TrueHD clips. No axis swap, inversion, offset or clamp.

rows.adm: `position Z`, omitted when 0 (profile)
rows.classification: omission = 0 per profile table 11
rows.note: Absent Z is read as 0.0 by the profile rule; the comparator keeps presence separate from value and found no mismatch.

rows.internal: kept beside the state (`Extras.distance`, round 5), not in `ObjectState`
rows.adm: none (profile forbids `absoluteDistance`; cartesian blocks)
rows.classification: not representable in DAMF or in the profile; declared as `distance-dropped` (D12); corpus never specifies it
rows.note: Harness C19 pushes distance 2.0 and infinity through `Timeline::push`: nothing reaches DAMF or ADM, and the ledger says so (adm `screen-reference-dropped` 1, timeline `distance-dropped` 2). The corpus carries `unspecified` only, so no real scene loses information today. A BS.2076 mode would not carry it either: `absoluteDistance` is in metres and no public source converts `distance_factor`.

rows.adm: written on active objects as Dolby's converters write it (ten decimals of the float32 factor); `0.0` + importance `0` on inactive
rows.classification: Dolby-identical (D1): follows Dolby's converters against the letter of profile table 11; Dolby's validators accept it
rows.note: The audit's C02 lost -6 dB, +3 dB, -inf and a mid-stream -12 dB change (3 losses). Since D1 oadec writes 0.0000000000, 0.2511886358, 0.5011872053, 1.4125375748, the strings Dolby's Conversion Tool writes for the same scene (equal), and the Conversion Tool reads them back as -6, +3, -inf, -12 dB (the last gain of each object). On real material every gain is 0 dB.

rows.adm: `width`=`depth`=`height`
rows.classification: uniform size preserved; Dolby writes the same triple (+`diffuse 1`)
rows.note: Uniform sizes 0.25/0.5/1.0 round-trip exactly in both oadec's and Dolby's ADM. The corpus never carries a non-zero size.

rows.damf: one scalar, the width (DAMF has no 3-axis size)
rows.adm: three identical values, the width (profile table 11 requires identical values)
rows.classification: the model keeps three axes; both formats carry one value, the width is written and `size-axes-collapsed` declared per event (D5)
rows.note: Harness C04 pushes size [0.2, 0.5, 0.8] through `Timeline::push`: DAMF and ADM carry the width (DAMF sizes per object: object 1: [0.2]; object 2: [0.5]), now declared (adm `size-axes-collapsed` 1, damf `size-axes-collapsed` 1). The width is the axis a uniform OAMD size sets for all three.

rows.adm: none (profile: `objectDivergence` shall not be used)
rows.classification: not representable in DAMF or the profile; declared as `divergence-dropped` (D12); no corpus stream carries it
rows.note: No test material exists and the authoring route cannot produce it; N/T, not PASS. The ledger's count is held by unit tests of `program.rs`.

rows.adm: omitted on active objects (profile), `0` on inactive
rows.classification: profile rule; Dolby drops it identically; declared as `importance-omitted` (D11), for the first state of a bed channel too (round 5); corpus always 1.0
rows.note: Harness C03 (importance 0.5 and 0.0 on active objects): 2 losses in oadec's ADM, declared (adm `importance-omitted` 2); Dolby's converter writes importance on 0 blocks for the same stimulus. Absent importance means 10 (BS.2076 default) = full priority, which equals the corpus value 1.0.

rows.source: OAMD: linear ramp from the update time (TS 103 420 5.6.2)
rows.adm: `jumpPosition=1` always (profile)
rows.classification: same shape (ramp starting at the event) on both sides
rows.note: BS.2076-3 section 9.3 and TS 103 420 figure 4 describe the same start-anchored ramp; the profile's `jumpPosition=1` is the right mode. The evaluator's self-check returns 0 against a synthetic ADM carrying the real ramps.

rows.adm: fixed: 0 on block 1, 250 samples afterwards (`INTERPOLATION_SAMPLES`)
rows.classification: profile rule (table 11 mandates 0 then 250); Dolby's converters write the same and Dolby's reader ignores any value; declared as `ramp-replaced` with the source lengths (D4); `--adm-interpolation real` writes the source ramps, marked outside the profile
rows.note: 36158 of the matched real-material blocks carry 250 where the DAMF ramp was 1536 (or 32/1152/1472). Dolby's Conversion Tool and DEE write {'0': 8, '250': 3278} for a stimulus cycling 0/32/250/480/1536/2048; every read-back through the Conversion Tool - of oadec's ADM, of a real-ramp variant and of Dolby's own ADM - returns rampLength 0 ({'0': 128}). Metadata-domain deviation up to 1.67 room units within one block per event; rendered by EAR the fixed ramp costs, against a real-ramp variant of the same file, fast-thd: 6.9-17.4 dB; pihead: 36.5-63.0 dB (min SDR per layout), while oadec and Dolby render bit-identically (7/7 layout comparisons).

rows.adm: `rtime` hh:mm:ss.fffff (10 us), `duration` rounded independently
rows.classification: sample-exact recovery
rows.note: Every ADM rtime decodes (nearest sample) to the DAMF samplePos: 0 time mismatches on 25 inputs incl. the whole film (30576 matched, 0 defects). 0 of 73014 timecodes fail to re-encode to the identical string. Blocks tile without gaps in the sample domain; rtime and duration are rounded independently (10-us `tile_dec` histogram all 0 on real material).

rows.adm: kept
rows.note: Against oadec's raw OAMD dump: 711 DAMF states and 694 ADM blocks fall exactly on OAMD update times (0 / 0 do not); 80 ADM blocks sit on times that only exist with the +32 term (21506 updates in the clips carry block_offset_factor 1).

rows.adm: block 1 at 00:00:00.00000 (profile); synthetic when the first event is later
rows.classification: corner case: real material always starts at 0; when it does not, oadec holds the first state from 0 and the real first event keeps its own block (D10), declared as `late-first-event-held`; Dolby writes a default (0,0,0) block then the real event
rows.note: The audit's C06: {'bed_event': 1, 'synthetic_block0': 2, 'absorbed_by_synthetic': 2}. Since D10 the arrival time is kept (adm `late-first-event-held` 2, adm `ramp-replaced` 2). Both behaviours invent something for a span DAMF leaves undefined. Not observed on any decoded stream.

rows.adm: last block ends at `frames`; audioProgramme end = frames
rows.classification: events at or after the end are dropped and declared, and the last block ends at the programme end (D8); block lists equal the Conversion Tool's
rows.note: Real material: last block ends at the programme end for every object (True), programme span = frames, DAMF frames = ADM frames. The audit's C07 found a block overrunning the end (1 object); since D8: adm `event-beyond-end-dropped` 2, adm `ramp-replaced` 1.

rows.adm: one block per event minus popped/superseded, plus synthetic
rows.classification: ledger identity holds; ramp-only changes become duplicate blocks or are popped
rows.note: `adm_blocks = states - superseded - beyond_end - trailing_popped - absorbed + synthetic` holds on every input. 73 duplicate blocks and 59 trailing pops on real material, all ramp-only changes the profile cannot express. No coalescing, resampling or rate limiting.

rows.internal: `Program.isf_objects` (the TrueHD count from the major sync, D2)
rows.damf: refused (exit 2); `--isf drop` writes the rest and declares `isf-dropped` (exit 4)
rows.adm: the same
rows.classification: no public source places an ISF channel: refused by default, dropped and declared on request (D2); no coordinate is made up
rows.note: The audit's C13 (4 ISF objects between the bed and 2 objects) lost the ISF tones in silence ([None, None, None, 100.0, None, None, None, None, None, None, 440.0, 880.0]). Since D2 such a programme is refused by name, or written without them on request: adm `isf-dropped` 4, damf `isf-dropped` 4. On real material N/T.

rows.adm: none (profile: DirectSpeakers blocks have no rtime/duration)
rows.classification: profile rule; Dolby's converters drop them identically; declared as `bed-event-dropped` and `bed-gain-dropped` (D11); corpus beds never change
rows.note: Harness C05: 2 bed changes lost, LFE PCM unscaled, declared (adm `bed-event-dropped` 2, adm `bed-gain-dropped` 1); Dolby drops the same (S8, static bed gain -6 dB also ignored). 0 bed changes lost on real material - none, because the LFE beds never change.

rows.adm: `RC_*` labels + table-10 positions; other channels refused
rows.classification: beds beyond 7.1.2 make `AdmWriter::create` fail explicitly (good), `Ls/Rs` of a 5.1 bed are labelled as side surrounds (untested on real material: all corpus beds are LFE-only)
rows.note: C14: `create: bed channel Tfl is not allowed in a Dolby Atmos master ADM bed` - an explicit failure, not a silent file. Zone rectangles equal the profile tables ([] findings). The LFE-only conformed bed passes every profile rule; with `--no-bed-conform` the LFE-only set is not one of table 16's configuration sets - and neither is Dolby's own output for the same DAMF.

rows.adm: objects numbered from `AO_100b` whatever the bed (D7)
rows.classification: profile table 17; Dolby-identical numbering
rows.note: The audit's C11 (no bed): ['profile-id', 'profile-id']. Since D7 objects start at `AO_100b` with any bed, as the Conversion Tool numbers them on the same programme (equal); the one decode of the audit that changed, the `--no-bed-conform` ADM of pi-head50m, changed in its object ids only.

rows.adm: `audioTrackUID sampleRate` = stream rate; 250-sample constant scaled
rows.classification: profile requires 48000 (table 23): refused (exit 2) unless `--adm-allow-non-profile-rate`, which writes it and declares `non-profile-sample-rate` (exit 4) (D6)
rows.note: The audit's C15 (96 kHz) was written without a word (findings ['profile-sample-rate', 'profile-sample-rate']). Since D6: refused; with the override adm `non-profile-sample-rate` 1, adm `ramp-replaced` 1. No Atmos material at 96 kHz exists in the library; the 44.1 kHz Pi encode is the only real case.

rows.adm: APR_1001 -> ACO_1001 -> AO_1001 (bed) + AO_100b.. (objects); custom DirectSpeakers pack AP_00011001; one Objects pack per object
rows.classification: identical element inventory and ids to Dolby's converters on the same DAMF
rows.note: Every produced ADM passes the reference-graph, chna and profile checks with zero findings (default conform).

rows.adm: one UID per PCM track; chna numTracks = numUIDs = channels
rows.note: Chain verified on every file; the negative controls show a dangling trackRef and a wrong UID sample rate are caught.

rows.adm: ebuCore 2016 namespace, BS.2076-1 timecodes
rows.classification: well-formed, references complete, profile-conformant; the profile's audioStreamFormat double reference makes strict BS.2076 readers (EAR) refuse the file - Dolby's own files included
rows.note: EAR renders only after the pack reference is removed from audioStreamFormat (applied identically to oadec's and Dolby's files); with that edit oadec and Dolby render bit-identically.

rows.adm: `RF64` FourCC, ds64 riffSize/dataSize/sampleCount, `fmt` tag 1 (24-bit), data, axml, chna, dbmd
rows.classification: RF64 (EBU Tech 3306) rather than the BS.2088 `BW64` FourCC; readers agree
rows.note: Whole-film Pi: 15278169042 bytes, RF64, ds64 = {'riff_size': 15278169034, 'data_size': 15266291040, 'sample_count': 242322080, 'table': []}; ffprobe 242322080, bwf_info 242322080, ds64 sampleCount and the DAMF all give 242322080 frames; 0 container findings. Both size thresholds (data above 4 GiB; data below but RIFF above u32) promote to RF64 correctly (harness C22, C22b).

rows.internal: three verbatim Dolby segments + bed mask + LFE flags + the warp mode with `--warp-mode stream`
rows.adm: required by Dolby validators; creator string gates acceptance
rows.classification: opaque; Dolby's validators accept the tagged file
rows.note: atmos_info 5.7.2 `--validate 1` and 1.1 accept oadec's ADM with `--dolby-origin-tag` (exit 0, no warnings) and refuse the default file on provenance only ('Content was not authored with Dolby tools'); bwf_info accepts both.

rows.source: OAMD may restate at one time; the timeline counts out-of-order events
rows.adm: same position: last wins (Dolby too), declared `same-position-superseded`; out of order: sorted and tiled (D9)
rows.classification: ADM sorts and tiles as the Conversion Tool does; DAMF is streamed, writes as delivered and declares `out-of-order-written-as-is` (exit 4) (D9); 0 out-of-order events on every decoded stream
rows.note: The audit's C09: {'objects': 2, 'gaps': 0, 'overlaps': 1, 'starts_at_zero': True, 'ends_at_frames': True, 'last_end': 96000, 'overrun_objects': 0, 'blocks_shorter_than_interp': 0, 'tile_dec': {'50000': 1}, 'unsorted_objects': 0}. Since D9: adm `ramp-replaced` 2, damf `out-of-order-written-as-is` 1. The CLI counts out-of-order events and reported 0 on every input of the audit.

rows.classification: a presentation other than 3 is refused with the object formats before anything is written (exit 2) (D13)

rows.damf: the ledger on stderr, one line per class; `--loss-report` JSON
rows.adm: the same
rows.classification: every lossy mapping is counted and printed (D3); exit 4 for a declared loss only; the report has a schema (version 2) and recorded goldens (round 5)
rows.note: The audit found no diagnostic for ramp, gain, importance, 3-D size, ISF, bed events, non-48 kHz or out-of-order input. Since D3 each is a kind of the ledger; round 5 brought it to 23 kinds. Every one of 27 writer-level cases meets its expectation (0 failures at the remediation; 0 of 27 again in round 5). Head cuts exit 7 for the truncated last access unit and the 96 kHz non-Atmos clip exits 2, both correctly.

rows.internal: written, kept beside the state, or counted
rows.classification: no OAMD field is dropped without a line (round 5); none of the new kinds sets an exit code
rows.note: Round 5 counts what used to leave in silence: `additional-table-data-dropped`, `alternate-object-data-dropped`, `unknown-element-dropped`, `bed-distribute-dropped`, `reserved-data-dropped`, `reserved-zone-read-as-all`, and a bed channel's first importance and trim bypass in ADM. No committed fixture carries any of them: their recorded loss reports changed by the `schema` field alone (13 lines) and their outputs are byte-identical to the round's base (25 of 25 runs). Field by field: `docs/oamd.md`.

rows.damf: `warpMode` with `--warp-mode stream`; none by default (read as warping)
rows.adm: `dbmd` segment 9 byte 152 with `--warp-mode stream`
rows.classification: the default keeps its bytes and declares `warp-mode-dropped` when the stream's mode is not the one the output reads as; kept on request
rows.note: Measured through Dolby's encoders: with the flag the mode survives the round trip; without it every mode becomes warping. TrueHD streams carry no trim element.

rows.adm: at most 118 objects and 128 tracks (refused before writing); 123 element instances counted
rows.classification: no file the writer makes exceeds a limit; the guard says so on stderr if one ever does and changes neither the file nor the exit code; which elements `MAX_ELEMENT_COUNT` applies to is read from the profile's wording, not verified against its table
rows.note: The largest programme the writer takes, a 7.1.2 bed and 118 objects, has 119 `audioObject` elements and no finding.

rows.classification: tool validation
rows.note: 22 of 22 injected defects fired the intended detector with no specificity violation ([]); not testable on this material: ['M-A10'] (no inactive block in pi-head50m; covered by harness C16).

rows.classification: Dolby validators: accepted (tagged); EAR: accepted after the profile's stream-format edit; Dolby Atmos Renderer not available
rows.note: EAR speaker outputs of oadec's ADM and Dolby's Conversion-Tool ADM are sample-identical in 7 of 7 layout comparisons over ['fast-thd', 'pihead']. Dolby's DRP cannot open ADM or DAMF files, and no Dolby Atmos Renderer is installed, so section 26/27 rest on the Conversion Tool, DEE, atmos_info, bwf_info and EAR.

scores.name: PCM fidelity
scores.basis: 590/590 track pairs sample-identical, whole film included

scores.name: Object mapping
scores.basis: chna chain and pairing matrix confirmed on every input; identity stable over time

scores.name: Bed mapping
scores.basis: LFE beds exact; multi-channel beds only via harness (labels/positions per table 10 confirmed); 5.1 `Ls/Rs` labelling untested on real material

scores.name: Coordinate fidelity
scores.basis: 0 mismatches at float32 precision; raw-OAMD mapping within 9.7e-05

scores.name: Gain fidelity
scores.basis: the gain of an active object written as Dolby's converters write it and read back by the Conversion Tool (D1); the profile text reserves `gain` for inactive objects

scores.name: Size fidelity
scores.basis: uniform size exact; the model keeps three axes, both formats carry one and the collapse is declared (D5); corpus never carries size

scores.name: Timing fidelity
scores.basis: sample-exact against DAMF and raw OAMD incl. the +32 term; 0 drift over 1:24:08

scores.name: Interpolation fidelity
scores.basis: mode right, length fixed at 250 by the profile; identical to Dolby; rendered loss against real ramps fast-thd: 6.9-17.4 dB; pihead: 36.5-63.0 dB

scores.name: ADM structural validity
scores.basis: 0 findings on every default-conform file; object IDs from `AO_100b` whatever the bed (D7); non-48 kHz refused unless asked (D6); element limits guarded (round 5)

scores.name: ADM semantic fidelity
scores.basis: everything the profile can carry is carried exactly, the gain included; what it cannot (ramp, bed events, importance, distance, divergence) is declared; ISF refused or declared, never placed

scores.name: Renderer interoperability
scores.basis: Dolby validators accept (tagged); EAR bit-identical to Dolby after the profile-conflict edit; no Dolby Atmos Renderer available

scores.name: Overall ADM export
scores.basis: a faithful Dolby-profile ADM of the decoded scene, equal to Dolby's own conversion, every loss declared (23 kinds) and the audit's writer-level defects fixed (D7-D10)

verdicts.Structural ADM verdict: VALID [was MOSTLY VALID]. Every default (bed-conformed, 48 kHz) file passes the container, reference-graph, chna and Dolby Atmos Master ADM profile v1.0 checks and Dolby's own validators (with the origin tag); objects are numbered from `AO_100b` whatever the bed, and a non-48 kHz programme leaves the profile only on request, declared.
verdicts.Atmos semantic fidelity verdict: MINOR SEMANTIC LOSS, DECLARED [was undeclared], on every decoded stream tested: PCM, positions, timing and identity are exact and the file is functionally identical to Dolby's own DAMF-to-ADM conversion; the only loss on real material is the profile's fixed 250-sample ramp, and the run says so. For scenes the corpus does not contain, what the profile can carry is carried (gain, uniform size) and what it cannot (3-D size, bed events, importance, distance, divergence, ISF) is named on stderr and in the loss report.
